nodes.notes: Serves an n8n-hosted form (Email, Company, Score). Each submission becomes one execution.

nodes.name: Required Fields Present?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.email }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

parameters.errorMessage: Missing required field 'email' on incoming lead.

nodes.name: Abort — Malformed Input
nodes.notes: Fails fast with a clear message; triggers the error workflow instead of processing bad data. Watch out: Fails the run on purpose so the Error Workflow fires. This is intentional, not a bug.

nodes.name: Score the Lead
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Score each lead 0-100 from simple heuristics Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Assign Round-Robin Owner
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Round-robin owner assignment Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Route by Heat
nodes.notes: Routes each item to one of 3 lanes: hot, warm + fallback. Watch out: Unmatched items go to the fallback output; without one they are silently dropped.

nodes.name: Hot → PostgreSQL + Instant Ping
nodes.notes: Runs a parameterized INSERT ... ON CONFLICT upsert — parameters are bound via queryReplacement, never string-interpolated, so it's immune to SQL injection. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Postgres connection. Host, port, database, user, password from your Postgres provider.

nodes.name: Notify Assigned Owner
nodes.notes: Posts a chat message into a Microsoft Teams channel — same role as a Slack notify, for teams standardized on Teams. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Microsoft OAuth2. Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.

nodes.name: Combine Lead Paths
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per lead (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

# Log form submissions with PostgreSQL

**Pattern:** Form Intake · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Form

## Overview

Starts when the form is submitted, and covers capture-forms work end to end across PostgreSQL, Microsoft Teams, Google Sheets and Slack.

It moves through 20 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. New Lead Form Submission
2. Required Fields Present?
3. Abort — Malformed Input
4. Score the Lead
5. Assign Round-Robin Owner
6. Route by Heat
7. Hot → PostgreSQL + Instant Ping
8. Notify Assigned Owner
9. Warm → Drip via Slack
10. Cold → Park in Nurture List
11. Combine Lead Paths
12. Fingerprint for Idempotency
13. Drop Already-Processed Items
14. Load Previous Snapshot
15. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
16. Stamp Completion Time
17. Persist Run Metadata
18. Summarize Run Stats
19. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
20. Send Summary to Microsoft Teams

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Microsoft Teams → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing capture-forms work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

New Lead Form Submission → Required Fields Present? → Abort — Malformed Input → Score the Lead → Assign Round-Robin Owner → Route by Heat → Hot → PostgreSQL + Instant Ping → Notify Assigned Owner → Warm → Drip via Slack → Cold → Park in Nurture List → Combine Lead Paths → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Microsoft Teams → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Microsoft Teams → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping PostgreSQL and Microsoft Teams aligned by hand for capture forms
- Intake checked for completeness before it is stored in PostgreSQL, for capture forms
- Capture forms work where "Score the Lead" is still a manual step before PostgreSQL
- Capture forms work that only reaches PostgreSQL when a form is submitted, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps PostgreSQL and Microsoft Teams in step for capture forms, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in PostgreSQL or Microsoft Teams are skipped, across all 23 nodes of this capture-forms build
- A failed PostgreSQL or Microsoft Teams call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 23 nodes in this capture-forms build
- Bad input stops the run for capture forms instead of landing in PostgreSQL
- Branches rejoin before PostgreSQL, so a capture-forms run reports once rather than 23 times

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; Microsoft OAuth2; Postgres connection; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Round-robin owner assignment happens right after scoring, before routing — every lead gets an accountable owner regardless of tier, so even a 'cold' lead parked in the nurture list is someone's responsibility later, not an anonymous row in a spreadsheet.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Change the hot/warm threshold values and watch the tier distribution shift.
2. Add a 4th owner to the round-robin pool.
3. Add a follow-up wait+check to the warm-drip branch, similar to the drip-ladder spine.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Postgres connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your Postgres provider.
_Gotcha:_ Managed providers usually require SSL enabled in the credential's options.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.
_Gotcha:_ Graph throttles with HTTP 429 — the retry setting on this node already handles it.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your capture forms process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- PostgreSQL: connect as a role that can reach only the tables below, not as the owner.
- Microsoft Teams: restrict the app registration to the target team; tenant-wide permission is not needed to post.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

**Do not log**
capture-forms payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
